key_concepts: Divergent plate boundaries move away from each other
Convergent plate boundaries move toward each other
Transform fault boundaries slide past each other
Divergent boundaries form rift valleys and oceanic ridges
Convergent boundaries can form volcanic island arcs and mountain ranges
Subduction occurs when one plate dives under another
The San Andreas Fault is a transform fault boundary
Oceanic-oceanic convergence involves one oceanic plate diving under another
Continental-continental convergence forms a collision zone
Divergence creates a zone of tension
Tectonic plates are large slabs of lithospheric rock
Faulting and folding are processes that shape Earth's geological surface
